summary: Chatral Sangye Dorje (1913–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (~1930–1941) and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, whom he also succeeded.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh (b. 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Visva-Bharati University, McMaster University, and Magadh University, and served in Thammasat University's Department of Philosophy and Religion (~1969–2000).

Chen-kuo Lin (b. 1950) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed his studies at Temple University in 1991. He held professorships at National Chengchi University (attested 1997–1999, 2014–2018) and posts at IIAS and Leiden University.
Cheng Huang has held academic appointments at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, UT Southwestern Medical Center, and Southern Methodist University.
Cheng Yen (b. 1937) is an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yinshun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a Japanology scholar who studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.
Chhime Rigdzing (1922–2002) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chhimed Rigdzin (1922–2002) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Choying Khyabdel. He served as Professor of Tibetan at Visva-Bharati University (~1954–1987) and conducted research at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~1964–1965).

Chi Chen Ho is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., studied under Hsuan Hua, and worked as a UCLA teaching assistant.

Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. from UCLA in 1993, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and served as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Chia Theng Shen (1913–2007) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions and held a post with the Buddhist Association of the United States (~1964–2007).
Chie Ikeya is a historian who earned a Ph.D. from Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.

Chien Y. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (through 2011) and James B. Apple, as well as under traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013).

Chien-hsing Ho is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).
Chih-fu Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007) and later as its honorary director.

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. at McMaster University under James A. Benn (attested 2014) and served on the faculty at Fo Guang University (attested 2016, 2026).

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) studied religious studies at Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto (~1907–1910) and at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941), Ryukoku University, Koyasan University, Hanazono University, and Yamaguchi University.
Chijun Hamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Taisho University and its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 1978).

Chikafumi Watanabe works in Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree from the University of British Columbia (attested 1994) supervised by Karin Preisendanz and a Ph.D. from the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura (1995).
